But what does equal time mean when you're closing in on 2027? Last week a bombshell announcement ahead of next Spring’s presidential elections: major online content creators will have to respect the same balanced air time rules as traditional TV and radio broadcasters during the campaign period. Here at France 24, we’re already testing the stopwatches and combing ove the guest list spreadsheets. Should podcasters, YouTubers and influencers be subjected to the same rules as us?

items.title: EU says 'strongly' rejects premise of new US tariffs
items.desc: The EU said Wednesday that it rejected the premise of new tariffs on its exports proposed by the United States and expected Washington to stick by a deal struck with Brussels last year. The US unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

items.title: In boost for Netanyahu, judges question corruption trial charges
items.desc: Judges in the long-running corruption trial of Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu handed his defence a major boost on Wednesday in recommending the prosecution drop one of the cases in which he is accused of bribery. The recommendations, which came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival, were immediately cheered by Netanyahu's right-wing allies who demanded the trial be brought to an end. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

items.title: Poland says will create no-fly zone at Ukraine border after repeated airspace violations
items.desc: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods. The no-fly zone is intended to allow Polish forces to quickly identify any Russian military aircraft and shoot them down if necessary. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

items.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
items.desc: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production -- the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. The duties, proposed at up to 20 percent, come over allegations the economies "are promoting production and capacity divorced from the realities of demand and market principles," a senior US official said on condition of anonymity. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight.

items.title: The ‘French Milei’? Presidential candidate David Lisnard aims to reshape France’s right wing
items.desc: Having secured reelection victory Wednesday as leader of France's mayors, Cannes Mayor David Lisnard turns once more to build on his recent bid for the Élysée. As his Nouvelle Énergie movement gains momentum, questions swirl over whether his campaign will reshape the French political landscape, or if his party will ultimately cosy up to the far right ahead of France’s 2027 race to the polls.

items.title: Turkey's deadly factory blast: 'Investing in safety costs more than letting people die'
items.desc: An explosion at a steel factory on November 9 in Turkey's Aliaga, near Izmir, killed 19 people. This tragedy follows several others and highlights the issues surrounding workers’ safety in Turkey, our Observers say. They also condemn the repressive responses from the government and the company.

items.title: Paris takes on masculinist movements
items.desc: As masculinist movements face their first major trial in Paris, the city has announced several initiatives to combat this ideology. The campaign aims to call attention to the real-world danger posed by misogynist groups online. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler takes a closer look.

items.title: 'Free' land and thriving businesses: French village defies rural decline
items.desc: As France's mayors gather in Paris for their annual convention, the decline in living standards and public services in both urban and rural areas is high on the agenda. Rural mayors, in particular, are concerned about the shrinking populations of their communities. But one small French town bucking the trend is Parlan, in the Cantal region, where the population has doubled and local services have flourished thanks to an offer of virtually free plots of land.

items.title: Moldova launches national preparedness campaign after drone incursions
items.desc: Moldova is urging its citizens to prepare for emergencies as the war in neighbouring Ukraine brings new risks across its border. The “Moldova Ready” campaign, launched in Chisinau, includes a display of the remains of a drone carrying 52kg of explosives after it crashed in the country last month. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

items.title: Top Spanish court closes case against Catalan separatist leader
items.desc: Spain's Supreme Court has applied a controversial amnesty law to former Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, closing criminal proceedings against him over his role in the region's failed 2017 independence bid. The ruling, which comes ahead of a snap general election on Sunday, marks the final step in the implementation of the amnesty law, passed by parliament in 2024.

items.title: Huang's return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop
items.desc: A rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's chief executive faded on Tuesday, with the company's shares falling as doubts persisted over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom. After vaulting more than 30 percent on Monday following Huang's shock comeback, Nvidia fell almost six percent Tuesday. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

items.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
items.desc: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production – the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. The new tariffs will need to undergo a period of public comment before taking effect. The new levies target some of the United States' largest trading partners. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

items.title: Iranian family seeks release of twin sisters facing death penalty and 25 years in prison
items.desc: Twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi are awaiting their sentences in Iran. They were arrested in January 2026, at the age of just 19, for taking part in protests against the Iranian regime. Taraneh is facing the death penalty, while Romina has been sentenced to 25 years in prison. Their family has been campaigning for their release.

items.title: Russian casualties in Ukraine war: New reports suggest death toll as high as 700,000
items.desc: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests some 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency.

items.title: Iowa: Toxic dust fears as US Army blows up 10,000 pounds of explosives
items.desc: An enormous explosion rang out across rural Iowa Tuesday as the US military carried out the controlled detonation of some 10,000 pounds of lead azide. US officials say the material, which was once used as a detonator in munitions, had become unstable and was at risk at risk of spontaneous explosion. But the risk of a toxic cloud of lead dust spreading out from the blast zone has caused public safety fears among locals.

items.title: Colombia: Security forces rescue hostages in supermarket siege
items.desc: Some 25 people being held hostage by gunmen in a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, were freed Tuesday after security forces stormed the building. One assailant was killed during the operation but no hostages were injured.

items.title: US Army detonates lead explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears
items.desc: The US Army on Wednesday blew up 5 tons of lead-based explosives at an ammunition plant in Iowa despite community backlash over fears of environmental contamination. The detonation was postponed three times, but got the green light after a federal appeals court this week found the US Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards to minimise the dispersal of lead dust.

items.title: 'We need to stop the war in Iran': US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal
items.desc: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Democratic Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal laid out her priorities for the new Congress: ending the war in Iran, tackling the cost-of-living crisis, curbing political corruption and holding the Trump administration accountable for its immigration crackdown. She also called for the "complete" dismantling of the US federal immigration agency ICE and backed an end to US military funding for Israel.

items.title: Libya’s Haftar visits old foe Turkey for first time in ‘new phase’ of ties
items.desc: Eastern Libya military commander Khalifa Haftar met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Wednesday during his first official visit to Turkey, marking a major thaw in relations between the longtime rivals. The visit came days after Ukraine struck a Russian warship in Benghazi, a port city controlled by Haftar.

items.title: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
items.desc: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Wednesday declined to comment on reports in Russian and international news outlets that around 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war so far. The reports were based on hacked data from Russia's official statistics agency. Peskov said only the defence ministry can disclose figures and told reporters "not to pay attention to any other data".

items.title: French Mayors Conference: 2027 Elysée hopeful Lisnard reelected association president
items.desc: The Mayor of Cannes, David Lisnard, has been re-elected president of the Association of Mayors of France, securing a comfortable victory in a vote announced on Wednesday. Lisnard is also a candidate in next year's French presidential election. For more on what his re-election could mean, FRANCE 24's James André reports from the Association of Mayors' convention in Paris.

items.title: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line
items.desc: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced to within about 60 kilometers of the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the southern city of Aden, but the forces fighting them have set up a fortified line to defend the city, a military official said Tuesday. The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory around the crucial waterway.

items.title: 安理会聚焦人工智能军事应用 古特雷斯和红十字国际委员会呼吁加强国际规范
items.desc: 联合国秘书长古特雷斯周二在安理会关于“技术快速变革时代下的冲突解决”高级别公开辩论会上警告称，人工智能正在进入战场，并带来自主武器、虚假信息和技术竞争等一系列和平与安全风险。他强调，人类必须始终掌握涉及生死的决策权，不能允许人工智能成为规避问责的借口，并呼吁紧急启动谈判，制定关于致命自主武器系统的具有法律约束力的文书。

items.title: 全球抗艾滋病进展面临威胁 资金削减可能导致疫情卷土重来
items.desc: 联合国艾滋病规划署周二发布最新报告指出，国际艾滋病防治资金削减、预防项目中断以及社区服务机构关闭，正在威胁数十年来全球抗击艾滋病取得的进展。如果各国无法弥补资金缺口、保障重点人群获得预防和治疗服务，艾滋病疫情可能再次蔓延。

items.title: 【专题报道】从温暖家庭到赋能产业：COP31释放全球地热发展潜力
items.desc: 提到地热，人们往往首先想到温泉。但在世界许多地方，来自地球深处的热量，正以更加多样的方式走进日常生活：它可以为千家万户提供暖气，为温室里的农作物创造适宜的生长环境，也可以服务工厂生产、食品加工，甚至为人工智能数据中心提供电力。

items.title: 古特雷斯呼吁就全球人工智能安全框架展开磋商，警告将出现历史性的权力转移

items.title: 全球仅7%的暴力幸存女性向警方报案   每小时5名女性遭伴侣或家人杀害
items.desc: 联合国妇女署和联合国毒品和犯罪问题办公室周一发布的最新数据显示，全球仅有23%遭受身体或性暴力的女性会寻求帮助，向警方报案的仅占7%。与此同时，2025年全球有47000名妇女和女童被亲密伴侣或家庭成员蓄意杀害，平均每小时5人遇害。联合国警告，司法体系未能有效保护暴力幸存者、追究施暴者责任，针对妇女和女童的暴力及杀害行为仍然普遍存在。

items.title: 独立科学小组：各国发展人工智能能力不必一味追求尖端模型
items.desc: 由联合国大会设立的人工智能独立国际科学小组周日发布的一份专题简报指出，各国提升人工智能能力并没有单一模式，也不必一味追求自主研发最先进的人工智能模型。无论选择使用现有系统、改造开放模型，还是从头开发自己的模型，关键都在于投资建设数据、算力、人才、工作流程和制度等基础能力。

items.title: COP31气候谈判无果而终：古特雷斯警告“科学不容置疑”
items.desc: 经过两周密集谈判和两天加时磋商，第三十一届联合国气候变化大会周日在土耳其安塔利亚落下帷幕。由于各方围绕化石燃料问题分歧严重，谈判陷入僵局，最终未能就气候协议达成共识。

items.title: 联合国有关管制“杀人机器人”谈判达成最低限度共识

items.title: 【世界进行时】2026年11月20日

items.title: 【前方视野】1.5摄氏度临界点逼近：中国如何回答气候变化时代的转型之问
items.desc: 从工业革命以来，人类从未像今天这样清晰地感受到自身活动与地球系统之间的关联。持续刷新的高温纪录、愈发频繁的极端天气，都在提醒国际社会，应对气候变化的窗口正在收窄。在土耳其举行的第31届联合国气候变化框架公约缔约方大会（COP31）上，各国围绕减排目标、能源转型、气候融资和绿色贸易展开激烈讨论。面对全球升温可能在未来十年内跨越1.5摄氏度关键门槛的警示，中国国家气候变化专家委员会副主任王毅在接受《联合国新闻》专访时表示，气候行动已进入更加注重落实的新阶段，而中国正在通过全面绿色转型、新型能源体系建设、绿色低碳技术创新及法律制度建设，为长期绿色低碳发展探索了一条具有自身特色的路径。

items.title: 约旦河西岸：定居者袭击事件创纪录  联合国敦促以色列保护农民

items.title: 粮食署计划2027年援助9100万人

items.title: 支离破碎的游乐场和冰冷的教室：乌克兰儿童遭遇最惨重的一年
